issue.title: Why  resubscribe the source observable emit same output when I use retryWhen operator?

REASONING: This issue is about understanding the behavior of RxJava's retryWhen operator and how it interacts with variable scope. The problem is conceptual in nature - the user is confused about why changing the value of the "str" variable inside the retryWhen operator doesn't affect subsequent retries. This is a fundamental concept about how RxJava's operators work - the source Observable.just(str) captures the value of str at creation time, not at subscription time. When retryWhen resubscribes to the source, it's resubscribing to the same Observable.just("aaa"), not re-evaluating the current value of str. This can be verified through code analysis without needing to build or run the code. The solution would involve explaining this behavior and suggesting alternatives like using defer() to re-evaluate the str variable on each subscription. This is a conceptual understanding issue that can be verified through documentation and knowledge of RxJava's behavior, not requiring actual execution of the code.
